chunks: Then He chose for Muhammad, peace be upon him, to meet Him, and was pleased with what is with Him for him, so He honored him by [removing him] from the abode of the world, and desired for him by [removing him] from enduring the trial, so He drew him to Himself with honor, peace be upon him and his family.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَهُ: Glory be to Him (referring to Allah)
key_terms.قَبَضَهُ: He drew him / He took him (referring to death/soul-taking)
key_terms.لِقَاءَهُ: To meet Him (referring to meeting Allah in the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia theology interpret the death of the Prophet Muhammad as an honor?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha frames the Prophet's death (Wafat) not as a termination but as a 'return' (Rujoo') to the Divine Presence, emphasizing his status as the chosen beloved (Habib) of Allah. Sharif al-Radi highlights the transition from the 'house of trial' (Dar al-Dunya) to the eternal abode, reinforcing the concept of the Prophet's bodily and spiritual ascension as a unique honor distinct from ordinary mortality. This perspective aligns with the Shia understanding of the Prophet's life as a continuous journey of divine selection, culminating in his gathering with Allah in a state of dignity (Karama).
